verdict.rationale: MotherDuck documents a way to restrict an AI assistant to read-only access on its MCP server, and it offers role-based read grants and include-pattern-limited Shares. Together these give some least-privilege control over what an agent can reach. The evidence never shows issuing a dedicated, scoped API token or credential for an agent, so the credential-issuance part of the story is only implied. Missing for 10: explicit scoped/read-only API token issuance, per-agent credential management (rotation/revocation/expiry), and independent or hands-on corroboration.
